children: Vodafone Idea shares fell on Tuesday after HSBC retained its ‘reduce’ rating on the telecom operator, warning that its operating cash flows are likely to fall short of spectrum payment obligations even as tariff hikes support earnings growth.

The Vodafone Idea stock was down 0.83 percent at Rs 15.47 in afternoon trade. The shares had gained around 7.7 percent over the previous two sessions. The stock is still up about 33 percent so far in 2026, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen around 9 percent over the same period. Vodafone Idea’s market capitalisation stands at about Rs 1.68 lakh crore.
HSBC maintained its ‘reduce’ call on Vodafone Idea with a target price of Rs 8.25 per share, implying downside of about 47 percent from the previous session’s closing price.

The brokerage’s key concern is Vodafone Idea’s ability to generate enough cash to meet its spectrum-related liabilities. HSBC expects the company’s operating cash flow to fall short of its spectrum payment obligations in FY29, even after factoring in a mobile tariff hike in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.

According to HSBC, Vodafone Idea would need to nearly triple its operating cash flow over the next three years to meet these obligations.

The brokerage expects the telecom operator’s network investments to help stabilise its market share, but does not see them translating into meaningful market share gains. It forecasts EBITDA to grow at a compound annual growth rate of around 15 percent between FY26 and FY29, driven primarily by the assumed tariff increase.

Funding requirements could extend beyond the FY29 spectrum payments. HSBC said Vodafone Idea would need additional capital for spectrum renewals beginning in 2030, leaving spectrum-payment funding as a key overhang on the stock.

The cautious brokerage view comes a day after Vodafone Idea received relief in a tax dispute. The Supreme Court on September 7 dismissed the Centre’s plea seeking to revive a Rs 363 crore GST demand against Vodafone Mobile related to the sale of tower assets to ATC Telecom in 2017. Vodafone Mobile subsequently merged with Vodafone Idea in 2018.

Meanwhile, Vodafone Idea reported a net loss of Rs 3,754 crore for the first quarter. Revenue rose 3.2 percent sequentially to Rs 11,689 crore, while EBITDA increased 3 percent to Rs 5,034 crore. EBITDA margin was broadly steady at 43.07 percent, compared with 43.14 percent in the preceding quarter.

title: Vodafone Idea stock slips as HSBC sees 47% downside, flags spectrum payment funding gap
